title: The Inquiry Stage Attempt Contract
what_this_is: One entry in the ledger of what an inquiry's machinery actually did: which stage, when it was
queued, when it entered external work, when it stopped, how long that took, what it read, what
it produced, and — the part this contract exists for — WHICH KIND of not-producing happened.
It is DATA because two runtimes read it: the coordinator writes attempts, and the workbench
renders a live stage stream from them. A vocabulary in one runtime is a vocabulary the other
paraphrases, and a paraphrased outcome is a product claim nobody reviewed.
not_this: Not the deliberation event log (`inquiry-interaction.v1`). That records what was CHOSEN and by
whom; this records what the machinery DID. Collapsing them would put 'the compiler returned
nothing' in the same list as 'the person chose option two'.
Not a capability receipt. A receipt says what an instrument produced; an attempt says that a
stage was entered and how it ended. A stage may complete while producing nothing.

outcome_notes.queued: the driver intends to enter this stage. Written before anything external is touched.
outcome_notes.started: external work has been entered. Persisted BEFORE the call, so a process that dies mid-call leaves this behind.
outcome_notes.completed: it ran and produced what it was asked for.
outcome_notes.thin: it parsed and its own declared coverage/adequacy check failed. NOT completed — a parse is not an adequacy.
outcome_notes.truncated: the producer stopped on its output budget. Whatever came back is a PREFIX, and a short result here is not evidence that there was little to find.
outcome_notes.empty: it ran to completion and produced nothing. Look somewhere else.
outcome_notes.refused: a law said no. Stop asking this of the machine.
outcome_notes.unavailable: the instrument exists and is not running. Try again.
outcome_notes.skipped: the budget or the branch excluded it. Nothing is wrong.
outcome_notes.error: it raised. Distinct from unavailable, which is a reachability fact rather than a failure.
outcome_notes.interrupted: a `started` attempt whose process did not return. The call MAY have happened. It is never silently retried.

laws.text: `duration_ms` is null unless both `started_at` and `completed_at` exist. Zero is a real measurement — a stage that began and ended within one tick of a controlled clock genuinely took 0ms — so zero may never stand in for 'we do not know'. A UI that renders an unknown duration as 0ms reports a fast stage where there was an unmeasured one.

The `started` attempt is persisted BEFORE the external call is entered. If it were written afterwards, a process that died mid-call would leave no trace of a call that may have been made and charged for.

A `started` attempt with no terminal successor is reopened as `interrupted` and the session stops. Model and capability calls are not idempotent; a driver that re-ran one would double a charge and could produce a second, different result for the same recorded intent.

A stage that returned valid, parseable output and failed its own declared coverage or adequacy check is `thin`, not `completed`. This is the single most flattering failure available to the chain: a truncated model response that happens to close its JSON is indistinguishable from an honest short answer unless the producer's own signal is read.
`input_counts` and `output_counts` record what the stage itself reported. Nothing derives a count from prose, from a length, or from a downstream artifact. An absent count is absent, not zero.

`summary` is a UI-safe sentence about the ATTEMPT. Model output is referenced through `output_refs` and `receipt_refs` and never copied here — a ledger that inlined prose would become a second place the reading is quoted, and the second copy is the one a reader would trust.
Every timestamp comes from an injected clock. A ledger that read a wall clock could not be replayed, and its duration test would have to exclude the field it exists to check.

substage_notes: A stage may report progress WITHIN itself — image 2 of 4, then a cross-image synthesis. Those
are substage events on the attempt, supplied by the stage through an injected observer.
The coordinator never imports a stage's internals to discover them; a stage that reports
nothing still has its declared floor recorded — the count of inputs selected and the call
topology it declared — because those are facts the coordinator holds itself.

what_this_is: Which route established that a producer stopped on its output budget. It is recorded because
the routes are not equally trustworthy and a reader is entitled to know which one answered.
`unknown` is NOT `none`: the first says nothing could be consulted, the second says something

truncation_source_notes.field: the producer's receipt declares it in a typed field. The only route that cannot be mistaken.
truncation_source_notes.producer_attribute: the producer object declares it as an attribute the coordinator reads directly.
truncation_source_notes.receipt_note: an exact, anchored `finish_reason: <value>` note the producer emits itself. Machine-written, not model prose.
truncation_source_notes.none: a route was available and reported no truncation.
truncation_source_notes.unknown: no route was available. Nothing is claimed either way.
